title: Deployment evidence is stronger than a shell transcript; rollback is evidence-driven
summary: DeploymentResult and DeploymentEvidence retain intent, initial/final observations, plan, action results, artifact hashes, executable versions/paths and verification. Rollback describes what can actually be reversed and never claims universal reversibility.
invariants: Retain enough evidence to answer what was intended, observed, changed and verified.
Action execution evidence and final verification evidence are distinct.
Secrets are excluded from ordinary evidence.
Every action declares reversibility before execution.
Rollback may be unavailable or provider-dependent and that fact must be explicit.

provenance.claim: Defines DeploymentResult and durable evidence content.
Defines evidence-driven rollback and explicit reversibility limits.
